settings.text: Constantly licking or nibbling at their rear end, often out of nowhere.

settings.repere: Paragraphe · A fishy smell that lingers, and poos tha
settings.text: A fishy smell that lingers, and poos that are soft, loose or all over the place.

settings.repere: Titre H2 · It all comes down to one cause
settings.text: It all comes down to one cause

settings.repere: Paragraphe · Your dog can’t empty their anal glands p
settings.text: Your dog can’t empty their anal glands properly. They're meant to empty naturally every time your dog poos, squeezed by the pressure of a firm stool. When stools are too soft or loose, that pressure isn't there. The glands get full and uncomfortable, and your dog starts scooting and licking to find relief.

settings.repere: Titre H2 · So how can you help your dog?
settings.text: So how can you help your dog?

settings.repere: Paragraphe · Start with their diet. Add more fibre to
settings.text: Start with their diet. Add more fibre to create firmer, bulkier stools that press on the anal glands and empty them with every poo. Support healthy digestion too — a balanced gut means fewer loose stools. Together, they stop the scooting and licking.
